howto.text: How to use this canvas — Tap any text to edit it. The bottom bar is one shared component (BottomNav): change it once and every screen updates. Press Play on a screen to click through the flow. Leave a comment on anything you want changed.

idea1.text: 1 · Needs-you queue — Everything waiting on the admin (unmarked attendance, substitutions, corrections, refunds, write-offs, data issues) lands in one Inbox tab with a badge.

idea10.text: 10 · Swipe on rows — Swipe a dues or student row for Call / WhatsApp / Note instead of opening the full profile.

idea11.text: 11 · Large text + dark mode — One toggle for older staff and evening use; the app's dark colours already exist.

idea12.text: 12 · Desktop next — The same Menu groups become a left sidebar, and Needs-you becomes a right-hand rail on wide screens.

idea2.text: 2 · Centre + button — Replaces today's Collect tab for the admin. Opens the 6 most-used actions: collect fee, mark attendance, send notice, add student, assign substitute, add note.

idea3.text: 3 · Search-first — One box finds students, receipts (by number or phone), staff, and actions like “collect fee for Aarav”. The Students tab opens straight into it.

idea4.text: 4 · Student 360 — One profile with fees, attendance, marks, notes and family. Entered once, reused everywhere. Teachers see it without the money card.

idea5.text: 5 · Role-shaped tabs — Same app, different bottom bar per role. Accountant keeps Home · Collect · Calls · More. Class teacher gets Today · My class · Attendance · Marks · More.

idea6.text: 6 · Bilingual menu — English label plus a small Hindi line on every tile (toggle it in the Menu screen's Tweaks). The language switch stays in the header.

idea7.text: 7 · Pinned workspaces — Admin pins up to 4 tiles to the top of Menu; pins are saved to the login, like the language setting is today.

idea8.text: 8 · 9:30 attendance check — After period 1, unmarked classes rise to the top of Today with one-tap WhatsApp reminders to class teachers.

idea9.text: 9 · Sync chip — When the phone is offline, a small “Offline · 2 waiting” chip in the header, so nobody re-enters attendance or a payment.

spec1.text: How to try it — Press Play on any frame: every frame is the same live app, opened at that screen. Approve and undo, remind teachers, collect a fee at the Payment Desk (type any amount, see where it goes, save), mark Class 9, switch on dark mode in Menu. All names and amounts are made-up sample data.

spec2.text: Motion — Screens slide in from the right and back out to the left in about a third of a second; tabs cross-fade; sheets rise from the bottom; list rows cascade in; rings, bars and the sparkline draw themselves. Only transform and opacity animate, the cheapest things for a phone to redraw. The phone's Reduce motion setting switches it all off.

spec3.text: Speed — Every action happens instantly and offers Undo: approve, reject, remind, collect, submit attendance. No spinners for things done on the phone. A receipt keeps Undo for 10 minutes, and undoing writes a reversal — receipts are never edited.

spec4.text: Thumb zone — What you press most sits in the bottom third: the + button, the Collect bar on Student 360, Submit on attendance, Review & save at the Payment Desk. Every target is at least 44 px.

spec5.text: Student 360 — Fee ring round the photo, pending-today vs not-due-yet, installment tracker, receipts with one-tap WhatsApp, October attendance calendar, exam marks with a Unit test / Half-yearly switch, parents and siblings with a family total, and which details are still blank.

spec6.text: Widgets used — bento stat tiles with sparkline and ring, live ‘now’ timeline, sliding-pill tab bar with badge, segmented controls with a sliding thumb, switches, swipe-left row actions, bottom sheets, snackbar with Undo, frosted sticky headers, number keypad, heat-map calendar.

spec7.text: Built to port — Uses the live app's own colours, fonts and dark theme (Inter, Source Serif 4, Noto Sans Devanagari). The motion is plain CSS, so it moves into the Next.js code in vppsone without adding an animation library.

spec8.text: Every module is now designed — see the Start here page, the area pages and the role app pages. The Menu tiles open them.

d1.text: How to try it — Press Play on any desktop frame. Click through the sidebar, sort the student table, tick rows for a bulk reminder, open a student, collect a fee at the Payment Desk (type the amount, date, mode and reference; check where it goes; save), approve items in Needs you and mark Class 9. All names and amounts are made-up sample data.

d2.text: Layout — A sidebar with a sliding highlight (it folds to icons on smaller laptops), a top bar with search and + New, then the page. Today keeps a right-hand rail for Needs you, the day's timeline and year pace. Student 360 opens as a side drawer, so you never lose your place in the list.

d3.text: Motion — Pages fade up, the drawer slides in from the right, dialogs scale in. Chart bars, rings and the heat-map draw in, and the bars morph when you switch 14 / 30 days. Cards lift on hover and the chart shows tooltips. The computer's Reduce motion setting turns it all off.

d4.text: Keyboard and speed — At the Payment Desk the amount box is ready to type as soon as a student is picked; Tab moves through date, mode, reference and notes, and one Save posts it. Search shows results as you type and Enter opens the first one. Every action is instant and offers Undo where the rules allow.

d5.text: Widgets — KPI cards with sparkline and ring, daily bar chart with an average line and tooltips, class × installment heat-map, payment-mode donut, sortable table with checkboxes and a floating bulk bar, side drawer, search dialog, two-pane inbox, class cards with a marking panel.

d6.text: Responsive — 1440 px: full sidebar and rail. 1180 px: icon sidebar. Under 1060 px: one column. Under 760 px the phone design takes over.

d7.text: All modules — the sidebar now opens every module and, under “See the app as”, the teacher, accountant and coordinator apps. Next: move this into the vppsone code, which needs that repo attached to a session.

intro-r-teacher.text: Teacher app — for Ms. Kavita Bhati (class teacher of Class 6, Science for 6/7/8). Built for people who are not technical: big buttons, icon + word, Hindi under every label and an EN | हि switch, one job per screen, friendly ticks and Undo, help on every screen. Teachers never see money.

intro-r-accountant.text: Accountant app — for Ms. Neelam Sharma. Collection works exactly like the live fee app’s Payment Desk: one student at a time, type whatever the parent paid, enter date, mode, reference and notes, see where the money goes, save once with certainty. Then deposit cheques, match UPI and close the day. Fee setup is view-only; waivers, reversals and refunds go to the admin.

intro-r-academic.text: Academic coordinator app — for Ms. Asha Purohit. Marks, progress and attendance across every class, with the children who need help found automatically, teachers’ notes and support plans, and one-tap reminders to late teachers.

intro-r-exam.text: Exam coordinator app — for Mr. Hemant Trivedi. Plans each exam (date sheet, seating, duties, papers), chases marks entry, and runs results day (grace, lock, report cards, publish, re-checks).

smart-r-teacher.text: Smart defaults — attendance starts with everyone present; “same as yesterday” in one tap; marks jump to the next child; last test shown faintly; leave pre-set to today · full day; notes can be spoken; follow-ups default to next Monday; report-card remarks are suggested.

smart-r-accountant.text: Helpers, never assumptions — nothing is pre-ticked: the accountant types the amount the parent actually paid. Chips only fill the box (overdue fees, installment balance, up to next installment, whole year). The app splits the money oldest first, shows the late fee apart, works the late fee out for a back-dated payment, warns about a possible duplicate, and locks the form once saved.

m-title.text: VPPS One — every screen, every role, desktop and phone

m-how.text: How to use this — Each page holds one area or one person’s app. Every module is a single responsive design: the wide frames are laptop/desktop, the 390 px frames are phone. Press Play on any frame and click; sidebars, bottom bars, menus and links move between screens. Leave a comment on anything to change.

m-start.text: Admin — Phone UI and Desktop UI pages hold the admin prototypes; the Money, People, Academics and Messages & system pages hold every admin module. In the admin sidebar and phone Menu, “See the app as” opens the teacher, accountant and coordinator apps.

m-roles.text: Role apps — Teacher app, Accountant app, Academic coordinator app and Exam coordinator app each have their own sidebar, bottom bar and home screen, showing only what that person needs.

m-rules.text: Rules kept everywhere — Pending today and Not due yet are never added together. Late fee is always shown apart. Receipts are never edited (reversal + Undo). Attendance starts with everyone present for the teacher, but a class counts only after Save — “not marked” never counts as present. Anything to parents is Hindi first with a preview. All names and numbers are made up.

m-notes.text: Notes on children — any class or subject teacher can speak or type a note about a child, tag it and ask for follow-up. It reaches the class teacher and coordinator, shows on Student 360, and can grow into a support plan.

m-motion.text: Motion — only transform and opacity, so it stays smooth on cheap phones: rows fade up in a stagger, screens slide forward/back, sheets rise (dialogs on desktop), ticks draw themselves, charts grow, the voice note listens with ripples and a live waveform. Reduced-motion settings are respected.

m-count.text: 30 modules · 235 screens and states · 315 frames on the area and role pages, plus the phone and desktop admin prototypes.
